controls.title: Ads Order Interfacing
controls.description: For Ads orders originating through Ads Manager or Deal Manager/Deal Booker, the applicable Ads services automatically validate and completely and accurately persist ad account, billing account, purchase profile, contract effective dates, and deal assignment information, as applicable, in Habitat for downstream billing and invoicing.

controls.title: Magic Link Generation
controls.description: Upon Billing Enterprise Syncer processing an Ads onboarding Salesforce order, Arsenal automatically creates or reuses a unique Ads onboarding intent, generates and sends a Magic Link to the customer, and automatically associates the customer data submitted through the link to the relevant customer account and billing fields in Ads Manager.
controls.notes: In follow up with Ankit for additional evidence (Task 3505)

controls.title: Terms and Conditions Acceptance
controls.description: Ads Manager prevents ads account creation unless the applicable Terms and Conditions have been accepted.

controls.title: Monetizable Event Qualification
controls.description: Baklava identifies and tags non-billable events (internal, test, expired) to exclude from monetization. Abacus (part of Mati Flink pipeline) validates billability of events (price, valid action type) and outputs monetizable events. The monetizable events are persisted in Databricks.

controls.title: Budget Chargeability and Final Monetization
controls.description: Ads Budget Enforcer calculates the chargeable amount for aggregated monetizable events based on budget, spend-to-date, and applicable budget rules.

controls.title: Post-Auction FX Currency Conversion
controls.description: After auction, Baklava converts the USD clearing price back to the advertiser’s local currency, floors and caps the amount at the local max bid, and carries local amount, USD amount, currency unit, and FX rate context downstream. Abacus preserves and validates the FX context for monetization and billing.

controls.title: Billable Amount Calculation
controls.description: The billing workflow worker, orchestrated via Temporal, automatically calculates billable amounts using Databricks data and transmits invoice intents to Invoicer to ensure accurate and complete invoice generation.

controls.title: Invoice Generation
controls.description: Upon receiving an invoice request from billing workflow worker, Invoicer automatically generates a draft invoice detailing the billing_account_id, purchase_profile_id, ad_account_id, associated contract/deal information, the effective billing window, currency, and the aggregated monetized amounts summed by campaign.

controls.title: Invoicer to Oracle
controls.description: For Ads orders routed to the Invoicer path, Ads Invoicer interfaces invoice data to Oracle completely and accurately for final invoice generation and billing.

controls.title: Billing Calculation / Credit Card Threshold Billing
controls.description: Credit card advertisers are billed when defined billing thresholds are met or exceeded and at month-end for any accrued valid impressions and clicks that amount to eligible outstanding balances.

followUps.description: Ads Manager enforces required campaign setup fields before campaign launch, including budget, flight dates, max bid, and campaign type.
followUps.question:
1. We have code evidencing the SofaAPI-to-Ottoman transmission of campaign data, however we cannot see that Ads Manager is the origin of this data. Is it possible to obtain code showing that Ads Manager calls to POST /v1/campaigns and POST /v1/ad_groups SOFA endpoints? If so, please provide names of relevant code files where this would be stored.

2. Our original understanding around the campaign set up process was that customers could configure campaigns within Ads Manager. However, evidence we received seems to indicate that "Arsenal" is the UI via which campaigns are configured and changed and that these changes are then applied downstream to Ads Manager. Can changes to ad accounts and campaigns be made via both Arsenal and Ads Manager? What is the relation between these 2 applications?

3. The code we inspected suggest that flight dates and billing event type are optional fields. Is there rationale for why these fields can be blank? Additionally, Max Bid seems to be conditionally required when bidding is set to "fixed bidding". What are the other bidding types and why is a max bid not required for these?

4. Attribute 2 for this control states that targeting should be a required field. Do we need to include "targeting" as a key field for this control? Our view is that targeting would not be key as it affects ad delivery, but generally does not directly determine the recorded monetary amount.

5. Can budgets be configured individually for accounts, campaigns, ad groups and individual ads? Is bidding only set at the ad-group level?

followUps.description: On a continuous basis, campaign, account, and budget data maintained in Habitat is completely and accurately indexed into Rockset through via a continuous, event-driven process facilitated by Habidex and Kafka.
followUps.question:
1. Is there any monitoring process in place over the CDC responsible for getting Habitat ad data into Rockset?

2. Based on the control description, we noted that this control is currently covering Ad Account (AdAccountOtm), campaign (CampaignOtm) and budget (BudgetPreferenceOtm) level data. It does not include ad group (AdGroupOtm) or ad (AdOtm) level data. Is there any rationale around this? Should ad group or ad level data be added into this control?

It appears that conversions are now a selectable option for customers in the campaign "bidding_type field". Are conversions now a billable event? If so,
a. Are conversions material?
b. If they are material, does the click control provide coverage over the conversions as well? Or do we need to scope in additional configs that track the conversions?
